_comment: Machine-readable migration manifest. A skill consults this to decide whether a project config needs updating; it must not judge for itself. See ../CONFIG_SCHEMA.md.

0.label: legacy
0.description: Pre-anchor layout. Config lives inside the docs directory; skills are rendered per project into .claude/skills/ with build-time placeholder substitution.

detect.note: Schema 0 records no version key. A config with no 'Config Schema' entry IS schema 0 — absence is the signal, not an error.

1.label: global-skills
1.description: Skills install once per machine to ~/.claude/skills/ and ship verbatim. Project facts live at the fixed anchor .specflow/config.md.

migrations.title: Move config to fixed anchor; list-valued commands; review gate; failure baseline
migrations.reason_not_auto: Command lists, the known-failure baseline and the review gate cannot be derived from a schema 0 config. Each needs confirmation. The file move and key renames below are auto; the rest are deferrable decisions.

moved_files.note: Source is git-tracked in consumer projects, so the move is reversible.

_renamed_keys_note: Schema 0 has no single canonical shape. cli/src/generate.js emits Format/Typecheck Command under '## Technical Layers', but configs written by the /init-specflow prompt place them under '## Tech Stack'. Both occur in real projects, hence from_any_of.
Readers must match on the key name and tolerate either section heading.

added_keys.source: derive as <Docs Path>/ROADMAP.md when that file exists
derive as <Docs Path>/SESSION_LOG.md when that file exists

merged_keys.note: Schema 0's mixed-stack shape, documented in prompts/INIT.md. Plural keys whose values are indented, labelled sub-bullets rather than a value on the same line:  - **Test Commands**:  /  followed by  '  - Python: pytest'  and  '  - DBT: dbt test'.
merged_keys.transform_note: Drop the 'Python:' / 'DBT:' label and keep the command. Merge with anything found in the singular Tech Stack > * Command keys, de-duplicating.
merged_keys.why_it_matters: This is the one schema-0 shape that already recorded multiple commands per category. It is also the easiest to lose: a naive line parser reads '- **Test Commands**:' as a scalar with an empty value and silently drops every indented sub-bullet. Dropping it would delete exactly the multi-command information schema 1 exists to preserve.

split_keys.note: Schema 0 encodes the format inline as 'jira (format: PROJ-123)'.

decisions.prompt: Schema 0 recorded one command per category. List every command that must run to verify this project — a single value silently skips suites.
decisions.on_defer: Carry the schema 0 scalar forward as a one-item list and annotate the config 'UNCONFIRMED: single command carried from schema 0'.

decisions.prompt: Record currently-failing tests as a baseline, with each failure's actual message.
decisions.on_defer: Write an empty baseline. Empty is valid and safer than a guessed one.

decisions.prompt: Probe for Codex and record the available review gate.
decisions.on_defer: Write 'none' and note that gated skills will announce they are running ungated.

decisions.prompt: The default ROADMAP.md / SESSION_LOG.md were not found under the docs path. Which files hold the task list and the session journal?
decisions.note: Not deferrable: Tasks File and Session Log are required in schema 1, and every session skill reads them. Deferring would write a config pointing at files that do not exist, which fails silently at the point of use rather than here.
decisions.applies_when: the derived default does not exist on disk

decisions.prompt: What commit message convention does this project use?
This project records a git workflow type schema 1 does not recognise. Is it solo or team?
decisions.note: Not deferrable: Type is required, and every session skill branches on it. Writing an unrecognised value fails silently at the point of use.

decisions.prompt: This project records a mode schema 1 does not recognise. Is it greenfield, adoption or constrained?
decisions.note: Not deferrable: the key is required and consumers branch on its value.

decisions.prompt: This project records a docs tracking value schema 1 does not recognise. Are the docs gitignored or tracked?
decisions.note: Not deferrable: the key is required and consumers branch on its value.

decisions.prompt: This project records a git platform schema 1 does not recognise. Which is it?
decisions.note: Not deferrable: the key is required and consumers branch on its value.

cleanup.prompt: Delete the per-project skill copies now superseded by the global install. List exactly what will be removed before removing it.
cleanup.note: These are git-tracked in consumer projects, so the deletion is reversible. Accepted consequence: a teammate cloning the repo gets no skills until they install SpecFlow themselves.
cleanup.preserve: Any skill directory not shipped by SpecFlow is project-authored — never delete it.

doc_changes.description: From schema 1, docs are agent-generated and populated rather than rendered from templates. specflow-init creates missing docs only; it never rewrites populated ROADMAP, SESSION_LOG or ADR content.

value_spaces._note: Every schema-1 key with a constrained value space, and how schema 0's vocabulary maps onto it. Machine-readable on purpose: migrate-config.js drives normalisation from this table and the test suite asserts the whole legacy space against it, so adding a value in one place cannot leave the other stale.

lossy.ci-cd-gated: schema 1 has no separate CI-gated type; the team workflow covers waiting on CI

Git Workflow > Type.why: end-session and rules/git-workflow.md branch on solo/team. An unmapped value matches neither, so the project silently gets no workflow instructions.

Git Workflow > Platform.why: Bitbucket was a schema-0 option that schema 1 did not list; it is a real platform, so the schema accepts it rather than the migration discarding it.

Integrations > Ticketing.why: Schema 0 wrote 'None' capitalised in every real project inspected, plus display labels like 'GitHub Issues'. Rules branch on the value being 'none', so the capital form reads as a configured ticketing system that does not exist.
Integrations > Ticketing.note: free_form: an unrecognised value is a ticketing system SpecFlow does not know by name, which is legitimate. It is kept verbatim rather than raising a decision.

comparison.skill_newer_than_project: Defer to specflow-init to migrate, then record the new version.
comparison.skill_older_than_project: The machine's SpecFlow is stale. Warn and proceed read-only. Never lower Config Schema — that relabels a newer config as older and destroys the mismatch signal permanently.

rules.write_policy: Write the config only when a migration actually changed something. A no-op check writes nothing. The config is git-tracked, so an unconditional version bump produces a commit-worthy diff on every machine after every release.
rules.session_policy: A mismatch found mid-session must not become a setup interview. Auto-apply changes marked 'auto'; offer 'decision' changes as deferrable. The task in hand always completes.
